notes: FIELDS ADDED TO SCHEMA.md (all optional, ignorable): nozzle.models = part numbers the chart row covers; rows[].gpmPrinted = the chart's gpm at the nozzle's own arc whenever rows[].gpm was scaled to a full circle; rows[].psiTo = upper end of a pressure BAND (Toro -PC nozzles are charted at '30-40' and '40-75' psi, stored as psi 30/psiTo 40 and psi 40/psiTo 75); rows[].widthFt/lengthFt = a strip nozzle's printed pattern at that pressure (radiusFt is null for strips); strip.corner = 'left'/'right' for corner and handed end strips; chartPrecip.psi = the chart row the precipitation pair was copied from; nozzle.arcRows = see next note.

ADJUSTABLE NOZZLES (Toro TVAN and PRN-TA; K-Rain KVF, KV, RN-ADJ, RN...-ADJ-90-210 and RN...-ADJ-210-270): the charts print separate rows for each arc setting, and gpm is NOT proportional to arc. 'rows' holds the full-circle equivalent of the rows at the nozzle's LARGEST charted arc (as printed when that arc is 360; PRN-TA = 270-degree rows x 4/3; RN...-90-210 = 210-degree rows x 360/210; RN...-210-270 = 270-degree rows x 4/3). 'arcRows' holds every printed row at every charted setting, with gpmAtArc = gpm AS PRINTED at that setting (not full-circle). Use arcRows (nearest charted setting) rather than scaling 'rows' whenever the head is set to another arc. The error from scaling can be large: at 30 psi TVAN8 prints 0.71 gpm at 90 degrees but 1.52 at 360 (scaling 360 gives 0.38); KV8 prints 0.40 at 90 but 2.00 at 360 (scaling gives 0.50); PRN-TA prints 0.19 at 45 (x8 = 1.52 full-circle) but 1.23 at 270 (x4/3 = 1.64).

FIXED-ARC SPRAY NOZZLES: rows.gpm = printed gpm x 360/arc, rounded to 3 decimals; the printed value is kept in gpmPrinted. Strip nozzles are in their own families with flow 'constant' (their printed gpm is the nozzle's whole flow and must not be scaled by an arc).

NOT PROPORTIONAL (as printed, transcribed unchanged): K-Rain FN-10F at 20 psi prints 1.03 gpm (the metric table agrees, 3.90 L/min) while FN-10Q x4 = 1.32 and FN-10F at 25 psi = 1.44 - looks like a misprint, treat the FN-10F 20 psi row with doubt. Toro PCD charts flows that keep rising with pressure (e.g. 5-TP 0.07 gpm at 40 psi, 0.19 at 70) despite the nozzles being 'pressure-compensating'. Toro Precision 10-Q prints 0.26 gpm at 20 psi but 0.23 at 30 psi, the only Precision row where flow falls as pressure rises (checked on the rendered page, and the 2022 catalogue prints the same). Smaller departures from proportionality are normal in all the fixed-arc tables.

PRECIP COLUMN ORDER differs between charts and was checked by rendering each page: Toro Precision/PSN+/PCD and PRN print square then triangle; Toro MPR Plus, TVAN, T5 and Mini 8 print triangle then square; K-Rain's 'n'/'p' glyphs are square then triangle. chartPrecip is null where the chart names no single reference pressure (Toro PCD, Mini 8, Super 800; all K-Rain rotors, whose recommended pressure is a range) or where the reference pressure is not a charted row (PRN: recommended 45 psi, charted 40 and 50).

TORO PRECISION (O-) SPRAY: the 2025 sell sheet 25-1045 tables are identical, value for value, to the Toro 2022 Specification Catalog pages 12-13 (cross-checked). Trajectories (5'=5, 8'=10, 10'=15, 12'=20, 15'=27, strips 20 degrees) come from the sheet's specification block, which covers PSN and PSN+; also applied to the PCD nozzles.

DOUBT - TORO 2026 RENAMING: Toro's 2026 sheet 26-1045 (https://cdn.thetorocompany.com/api/assetstorage/623_40a88c26-9e2a-4212-918c-b86a065f0536) renames the line PSN (PSN5-Q, PSN5T-Q ...), and its chart sheet PSN-SS-CHARTS26-ONLY (https://cdn.thetorocompany.com/api/assetstorage/623_0a983555-fa05-4587-b85c-a7a2c67a0e4e) prints, for the Q/H/F arcs at 30-50 psi, the PSN+ (Debris Guard) numbers, while its 20 psi rows, its other arcs, and 15-F at every pressure keep the O- numbers. It is not clear whether a nozzle sold in 2026 as 'PSN' performs like to-psn or like to-psn-plus. This file keeps the two clearly labelled 2025 tables: to-psn (O- part numbers) and to-psn-plus (PSN+ part numbers).
TORO PSN+ side strips PSN4X18-SST and PSN4X30-SST are in the model list but not charted: omitted.

TORO PCD (pressure-compensating Precision, 'P' suffix, recommended above 40 psi) comes from the US 2022 Specification Catalog pages 10-11; the 2025 PSN sheet no longer charts it. A 2016 metric EMEA PCD sheet (https://cdn.thetorocompany.com/api/assetstorage/623_37cb9b68-69d6-4392-adf1-abf925b5bb87) gives different numbers and says 60/150/210 degree arcs are not made with PCD; the US 2022 chart charts them, and the US chart was used.

TORO 570Z PR/PRX and 570S-PR/PRX bodies do not list the PCD or -PC families: Toro says 'Do not use PCDs with 570Z PR & 570Z PRX models'. 570Z LP (low pressure) bodies are rated 15-75 psi, the others 20-75. Check-valve (-COM), effluent and other option variants share their base body's entry.

TORO 570 MPR Plus: the 8' flat-spray nozzles FSQ/FSH/FSF and their -LG low-flow versions are in the model list but not charted: omitted. The special-pattern chart prints a single precipitation column for strips: not stored. Strip trajectory 17 degrees. The 2022 catalogue's text says MPR Plus nozzles have a 'pre-installed Pressure Compensation Disc' but its chart and model code treat -PC as an option; both are given, as separate families.

TORO TVAN: the chart's footnote says 'Data based on 360' although its gpm clearly differ by arc setting (see ADJUSTABLE NOZZLES). The catalogue does not state the TVAN's thread; it is listed on the 570Z bodies because Toro files it with the 570Z spray products, unconfirmed.

TORO PRN: the newest chart found is the 2020 sheet 20-1083. trajectoryDeg is null because PRN is multi-trajectory ('maximum trajectory height of 20 degrees'). An older version quotes 0.55 in/h matched precipitation, the 2020 sheet 0.6.
TORO T5 (2022 catalogue): precipitation 'based on 180 degrees', recommended 45 psi. Check-valve (CK), effluent (E) and no-nozzle (-LN) variants share the base body's entry.

TORO MINI 8: the specification block says arc 40-360 while a callout on the same page says 45-360; 40 used. Its pop-up to the nozzle is 3 3/4 in (stored as the model's nominal 4). The 1.5 nozzle's 30 psi row prints precip triangle 0.24 / square 0.30, the reverse of every other row (not stored).

TORO SUPER 800: the only chart found is the 2003 quick guide (form 373-0152 Rev B); the Super 800 is not in Toro's 2022 catalogue and is probably discontinued. The guide gives no minimum arc (arcMin null), no trajectory and no precipitation. Its chart is identical, row for row at 30-60 psi, to K-Rain's ProPlus chart, which looks like the same rotor design. Both print nozzle '1' at 1.3 gpm (30 psi) and nozzles '2' and '2.5' only 0.1 gpm apart; transcribed as printed.

K-RAIN: everything comes from the 2026 English product catalogue on krain.com. RPS 75 is a 3/4 in rotor, not a spray body, and is filed here as a rotor. The RPS75-6INCH-PR body is regulated to 45 psi (regulatedPsi 45), but K-Rain's separate PR chart shows each nozzle levelling off at its 50 psi row; the PR chart is not stored separately. RPS75-360 and RPS75-360-SH run full circle only, so the family's arcMin of 40 applies only to the adjustable bodies. The RPS 75 low-angle chart is identical to the ProPlus low-angle chart, as printed.

K-RAIN PRO-S: popUpIn is the model's nominal height (2/3/4/6/12); the catalogue's measured pop-up is 1 1/2, 2 1/2, 3 1/2, 5 1/2 and 11 1/2 in. Pro-S 'accepts female threaded nozzles', so it lists K-Rain's female-thread lines (FN, KVF, RN, RN-ADJ). KV and P12/P15 are male-thread nozzles, made for bodies like K-Rain's K-Spray, which is outside this group. Stop Flow (-SF), check-valve (-CV), nozzle-guard and reclaimed-water variants share their base body's entry.

K-RAIN STRIPS: the FN-15HL / P15HL high-low strip is omitted because its two-part high/low pattern does not fit the strip object. For the FN-15 strips, the nominal size is taken from the 30 psi row (the recommended pressure); for the RN strips it comes from the model names (515 = 5x15, 530 = 5x30). Each row keeps its printed W x L.
K-RAIN RECOMMENDED PRESSURES used for chartPrecip: Rotary Nozzle Series 40 psi; RN-ADJ, KVF, KV and FN 30 psi.
NOT TRANSCRIBED (outside this group's list): K-Rain NP and K-Spray bodies, the RPS 46/50/75i, Select, SuperPro and ProSport rotors; Toro 300/640/TS90 stream and golf rotors; Toro bubblers.

ORBIT - NOT FOUND: Orbit publishes no performance charts on orbitonline.com. Its product pages give only radius and nominal nozzle sizes: Voyager II 55661 '25 to 52 ft'; nozzle rack 55071 with 1.0/2.0/3.0/4.0 gpm standard nozzles ('radius of 35 ft'), 0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0/3.0 low-angle nozzles ('throw of 25 ft') and an 8.0 gpm pasture nozzle; adjustable spray nozzles '4/10/18 ft at 30 psi'. The Voyager II instruction PDF (https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0489/2445/9176/files/Voyager_Instructions.pdf) is a printer's proof of the English panel only and refers to a 'Nozzle Specs' panel that is not in it; the plumbersstock copy of the 55070 sheet is behind Cloudflare. No Orbit 'Eco-Rotor' product or chart was found (searches return Hunter's Eco-Rotator, a different product). The Voyager II body is listed with no nozzle families. Orbit calls its rack 'compatible with Voyager, Voyager II, and Hunter PGP'; that is a fit, not a statement that the flows match Hunter's charts.
